prompt: Write `reverse_string(s)` that returns the string reversed.

solution_steps.title: Reverse slice
solution_steps.what_it_does: Walks the string from end to start.
solution_steps.how_it_runs: The -1 step reads characters in reverse order.

solution_final_thought: Slicing is the idiomatic way to reverse sequences in Python.

prompt: Write `count_vowels(s)` returning how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) are in the string.
reference_solution:
def count_vowels(s):
    return sum(1 for c in s.lower() if c in 'aeiou')

hints.hint: Lowercase the string so case doesn't matter.
Loop over characters and count those in 'aeiou'.

solution_steps.title: Count matches
solution_steps.code: sum(1 for c in s.lower() if c in 'aeiou')
solution_steps.how_it_runs: A generator yields 1 per vowel; sum totals them.

prompt: Write `is_palindrome(s)` returning True if the string reads the same forwards and backwards, else False.

hints.hint: A palindrome equals its own reverse.

solution_steps.title: Compare to reverse
solution_steps.what_it_does: Checks equality with the reversed string.
solution_steps.how_it_runs: If reversing changes nothing, it's a palindrome.

solution_summary: Compare the string to its reverse.
